source: ALEX - Historische Rechts- und Gesetzestexte, Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek (alex.onb.ac.at)

source: FamilySearch full text - the compound "LERENA LERENA", the sharpest test of the central question

Nobody had ever searched for it. *** Run first against the Uruguayan Catholic registers (4 hits) and then against the whole corpus without a country filter (43 hits). *** EVERY SINGLE ONE IS A TRANSCRIPTION DOUBLING at a line or page end *** - "Pio Lerena . Lerena", "Zelmira Lerena , Lerena argentino", "Celidonio B. de Lerena Lerena", "G. Lerena Lerena" across a printed title page. Each was opened and each transcript read. This LOWERS the probability that Maria Lerena was a Lerena by birth; it does not close it *** - a woman can be a Lerena by birth without her children ever being written so, and Rosario's parish books are thin in full text.
tier: SECONDARY - a controlled negative across 43 opened documents

source: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo - Marriage Dispensation Records, July-August 1911

source: Iglesia Matriz de Montevideo - baptism of 30 June 1789

Twice, fifteen years apart. *** The act calls him SANCHO.

source: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, Montevideo - baptism of 12 May 1827

SANCHO LERENA y de Dona MARIA FERNANDEZ." *** Set beside the 1827 act it shows that "Antonio Rodriguez" and "Antonio Ruiz de Carvallo" are ONE MAN whose first surname the registers write two ways - so there is ONE Dominga, not two. *** The archive had held the two records apart, unmerged, precisely until an act joined them.

source: England, Devon, Parish Registers (Devon Record Office), 1529-1974

Agnes Walker Taylor, Devon 1918; and HORACE ARCHIBALD TAYLOR m. MARY JANE MARSHALL, banns NORTHAM 17 Dec 1893. *** TWO SISTERS MARRIED AT NORTHAM ELEVEN DAYS APART in 1900, four months after their mother's death. *** *** The method matters: TAYLOR returns 705,979 results in England, so the RARE surname must be the principal and Taylor the spouse - and where both are common, the sisters' distinctive forenames do the work.

source: England and Wales, Censuses of 1871, 1901 and 1911 - the Taylors of Bideford and Northam
used_for: *** THE 1871 CENSUS SETTLES A QUESTION THIS ARCHIVE HAD WRITTEN DOWN AND LEFT: *** it has KATHLEEN GEORGINA and WILLIAM JOHN both as infants in the house on 2 April 1871, and their parents' banns were called at Bideford on 9 January 1870 - so they are TWINS, born November 1870, and the family had TWO sets of twins. *** THE 1901 AND 1911 CENSUSES NAME WILLIAM JOHN'S WIFE AS "FANNY HELEN" and date the marriage to 1892 *** - where a tree said "Fanny Ellen JEFFEREY", a surname no record supports. *** AND THEY SHOW TWO OF THE TEN SIBLINGS IN THE SAME CORNER OF SOUTH DEVON: *** William John at PAIGNTON by 1911, Lucy Elizabeth's banns at CHURSTON FERRERS three miles away in 1909, both eighty miles from Northam where they were born. The brother was there first.

source: FamilySearch full text - the Rosario films, tested for transcripts rather than assumed

The DEATHS film, DGS 4531019, is NOT transcribed and covers only 1731-1864, so it cannot hold anyone this archive is chasing. *** AND A HARD LIMIT: unquoted terms are OR'd, not AND'd *** - "Lerena Rosario difunto" returns 17,782,105 documents - so full text accepts exactly ONE quoted phrase and narrowing must be done by choosing a rarer phrase, never by adding words. *** The place facet is a trap: f.recordPlace on a full-text query returns a confident ZERO with "No filters available" against every heading. *** The third false-null caught on this service in one day.

source: Catedral Nuestra Senora del Rosario - Confirmation Records, DGS 4531018 item 1, images 5-80

source: FamilySearch browse - the FIVE FILMED PARISHES OF ROSARIO

used_for: *** NOT BLOCKED TODAY, and it answered a question this archive had spent the day calling unanswerable. *** Two Spanish archive indexes - "Index des mariages catholique de Grenade" and "Spain, Marriages, 1565-1950" - carry *** SANCHO LERENA y ARMENTA married to ANA MARIA DE AGUILAR, Diocese of GRANADA, between 1725 and 1775. *** A son of that couple would be styled LERENA y AGUILAR, which is exactly the name the trees give the Sancho born in 1767 - *** so "Aguilar", unattested across all fourteen Uruguayan records, is a real Spanish matronymic pointing at a grandmother, not a tree's invention. *** Index read, image NOT opened, and the date range is a fifty-year span, so it is a testable lead and nothing more. Geneanet also gives GRANADA against the trees' CORDOBA (ckurti: ZUHEROS, Cordoba) where the census says only ANDALUZIA; a DEATH IN 1832 for Sancho from four trees, where this archive has none; and his wife more fully as MARIA JOSEFA (TERESA) FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS. *** AND THE CENTRAL NULL HOLDS ON A THIRD PLATFORM: "Juan Carlos Lerena" returns exactly ONE result in all of Geneanet, a "del Campo Lerena" in which Lerena is the second surname. He is absent from FamilySearch, from WikiTree and from Geneanet alike. ***
tier: SECONDARY - trees and indexes read, no image opened

source: FamilySearch - the 1754 Granada marriage, and the Madrid notarial full text
used_for: *** THE GRANADA ACT, FOUND - and it collapses Geneanet's fifty-year span to a single day. *** Index entry ark 1:1:C9WG-BGW2: *** SANCHO DE LERENA Y ARMENTA, born CORDOBA, son of SANCHO DE LERENA Y VELASCO and MARIA ANTONIA DE ARMENTA Y GUEBARA, married ANA MARIA DE AGUILAR of LA MALA, daughter of FRANCISCO DE AGUILAR and BEATRIS FRANCO, at SANTA ANA, GRANADA on 17 NOVEMBER 1754. *** A second index entry for the same event sits in the Granada Pre-Marriage Investigation Files (ark 1:1:XPG2-RYP). *** BOTH ARE MARKED "IMAGE UNAVAILABLE" - the act itself is still unread. *** It also closes a tension this archive had open: the trees said CORDOBA, the marriage index said GRANADA, the census said ANDALUZIA. He was BORN at Cordoba and MARRIED at Granada, and all three were right. *** THE FULL TEXT THEN CARRIED IT FURTHER. *** "Lerena y Armenta" returns 55 hits - Madrid notarial records *** 1766 to 1808 ***, so the groom became a vecino of MADRID; and Cordoba nobility records, where a testament of *** 14 June 1751 *** is witnessed by *** DON ANTONIO DE LERENA Y ARMENTA ***, a brother. *** AND THE LOAD-BEARING FIND: *** a Madrid notarial act of *** 27 March 1790 *** (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2C-N7RV) is signed, in the signature position between the witnesses and the notary, by *** JUAN DE LERENA Y AGUILAR *** - one man bearing the compound. *** So "Lerena y Aguilar" is a name real people bore, in that family and that generation. *** A FALSE FRIEND WAS CAUGHT IN THE SAME SWEEP: the one MONTEVIDEO hit for that phrase reads "padrinos MAURICIO LERENA Y PETRONA AGUILAR" - two godparents, "y" meaning "and". *** NOTHING HERE JOINS ANY OF THESE PEOPLE TO THE URUGUAYAN SANCHO OF 1767. *** A controlled search for children of the couple in Spain returned a genuine null against a control of 12. *** And the one search that would have settled it - the exact phrase "Sancho de Lerena y Aguilar" - rendered "(0)" with no "No Results Found" line and no control, and the next request returned "Access Denied - Error 15". THAT ZERO IS NOT RECORDED AS A NULL, and re-running it with a control is the first job when the block lifts. ***
tier: SECONDARY for the marriage index; PRIMARY for the Madrid and Cordoba full-text transcripts read here

source: Geneanet - the jfina tree's sourced note, and Apolant's ficha 355
used_for: *** THE SOURCE BEHIND THREE DAYS OF THIS ARCHIVE'S ASSUMPTIONS, AND IT OVERTURNS ONE OF THEM. *** With FamilySearch blocking this session ("Access Denied - Error 15"), the 1791 act could not be chased on its films. Geneanet was open. The jfina tree (Josefina Sanchez Abal) carries a long sourced note on Sancho: *** born Cordoba c.1767, son of FELIX LERENA and ROSALIA AGUILAR, "c.m. 8.1.1791", citing APOLANT, "Operativo Patagonia" (Montevideo, Imprenta Letras, 1970), FICHA 355. *** *** THAT KILLS THE GRANADA HYPOTHESIS THIS ARCHIVE BUILT THE SAME MORNING: *** "Aguilar" is his MOTHER's surname, not a grandmother's from the 1754 Granada marriage, and the controlled null against that couple is explained rather than mysterious. *** IT ALSO SEPARATES THE DATE FROM THE PLACE: *** the date is Apolant's and published; *** "Canelones" is in none of it *** - the note's "Concejo de Morcin, Asturias" is the BRIDE'S birthplace, JOSEFA FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS b.1778, an ASTURIAN of the Operativo Patagonia convoy, which is why "Tresguerras" appears in no Uruguayan index. *** AND IT QUOTES THE 1812 PADRON IN FULL *** (AGN, Fondo ex AGA, L 251): calle San Juan No 60, Sancho "andaluz" 45, Maria Fernandez 36, six children all "naturales del Canelon" - Juan Agustin 21, Pedro Antonio 19, Agustina 17, Fidel 12, Justa 10, Dominga 7 - *** the father-in-law RODRIGO FERNANDEZ, 63, asturiano, in the household, and FOUR ENSLAVED PEOPLE. *** Two corrections follow: *** Juan Agustin was 21 in 1812, not a child ***, so this archive's own objection to reading the 1812 godparents "Juan Agustin SERENA y Agustina PERENA" as LERENA is withdrawn; and *** DOMINGA is in the census and missing from the tree ***, which the acts read here had already caught. Two further published citations noted and not yet opened: *** Revista 15 IEGU pp.53-54 ***, and Francisco Bauza, "Historia de la Dominacion Espanola" (1929) III p.285, placing *** the Lerenas of Canelones as trusted men of the BARON DE LA LAGUNA in 1817. ***
tier: SECONDARY - a user tree, but one that cites a named published work with a numbered ficha

source: Francisco Bauza, "Historia de la Dominacion Espanola en el Uruguay" (archive.org, full text)
used_for: *** THE LERENAS OF CANELONES ENTER THE NATIONAL HISTORY ONCE, IN 1817, AND IT IS NOT A CREDIT. *** The jfina tree cited Bauza III p.285 for the Lerenas as "persona de confianza del Baron de la Laguna... para vigilar la seguridad y tranquilidad". *** The tree quotes Lecor's euphemism and stops where Bauza's judgement begins. *** The Bando of 15 February 1817 outlawed resisting Orientals "ellos, sus familias y sus propiedades", with detachments to burn their farms and put their families aboard the fleet; "personas de confianza" were to identify them. Bauza then writes: *** "Doloroso es manifestar que las mencionadas personas de confianza, fueron los hermanos Alonso de Minas, LOS LLERENA DE CANELONES, ... quienes al frente de grupos cuya totalidad sumaba mas de 400 hombres, se transformaron en azote de los vecindarios de Toledo, Manga y Piedras, haciendo impunemente con ellos, lo que era castigado como un crimen en los patriotas." *** *** Bauza names a FAMILY, in the plural, with no forenames *** - so no individual in this register is placed at those events; but this archive's Llerena were at Canelones in exactly that generation, Sancho aged 50 and three sons grown. *** Thirty years before the Oribe material this archive already holds, and on the other side of the national story. *** The same volume has a D. JOSE PEREIRA LERENA serving in Rondeau's PATRIOT army - a different compound surname, recorded so nobody attaches the wrong man in either direction. *** Tomes I and II hold no Lerena at all - a controlled null, the word Montevideo returning 108 and 503 hits in the same files. ***
tier: PRIMARY for the text of a published work; SECONDARY as history

Recorded as a conflict. *** AND IT WAS OPENED TO TEST A CANDIDACY THE ARCHIVE HAD ALREADY CLOSED ON 17 SEPTEMBER. ***

CARLOS LERENA y ADELA CARNIGLIA, *** orientales ***, domiciliados en este Curato' - *** SO CARLOS LERENA IS URUGUAYAN ***, and four of that drawer's traceable fathers are now Uruguayan or married in Uruguay. *** AND AN ABELINO LERENA STOOD GODFATHER BY PROXY *** through Domingo Simois, which turns a suggestive forename into a man. *** WHICH AVELINO IS NOT ESTABLISHED: *** this register holds four of the name, and the adjacent Arturo row of cajon-985-origins.tsv was once attached to one of them and withdrawn the same day. *** NO AI TRANSCRIPT EXISTS FOR THIS IMAGE ***, so every word here is off the plate. *** THE WAYPOINT WAS CHECKED BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN DOWN: *** Q633-3DR is 'mendoza, Bautismos 1899-1903' in the Record Atlas's own volume data, and the act is 1900.

source: Santiago Apostol y San Nicolas (la Iglesia Matriz de Mendoza), Argentina - Baptism Records 1901-1903, printed-form baptism of 23 April 1902; FamilySearch DGS film 004597291 item 003, image 95, ark 3:1:939X-HFTB-Z; plate read at full resolution
used_for: *** THE ACT THAT TURNED A NATIONALITY INTO A CITY. *** Where the 1900 act could only say 'orientales' because it is prose, this one is a *** PRINTED FORM with a 'natural de' blank beside each parent *** - and both blanks read *** MONTEVIDEO ***. *** SO CARLOS LERENA, one of the four fathers /open-questions/ asks strangers about, IS A MONTEVIDEAN. *** It also gives *** MARIA MERCEDES LERENA, born 10 March 1902 in the city of Mendoza ***, and two godparents: *** D. EDUARDO CARNIGLIA *** in person and *** Dona MERCEDES LERENA DE MARTINEZ *** by proxy through the child's own mother. *** THE PROXY IS THE EVIDENCE: a godparent who must be represented lives somewhere else. *** *** SHE IS NOT IDENTIFIED *** with any of the three Mercedes Lerenas of Montevideo in this register, nor with the CAROLINA LERENA de MARTINEZ already here. *** THE LESSON FOR ANY ARCHIVE: WHEN A PARISH SWITCHES TO A PRINTED FORM, GO BACK AND RE-ASK THE QUESTIONS THE PROSE COULD NOT ANSWER. ***

Nationality is recorded for the deceased only.

used_for: *** A SECOND ARGENTINE MILITARY DRAWER, AND A DIFFERENT RECORD CLASS FROM CAJON 985 *** - fingerprint cards rather than enrolment fichas. It was reached through the PERSON and not through the drawer, which is why this archive had never opened it. *** IT CORRECTS THREE INDEX ERRORS AT ONCE: *** the surname is *** LERENA *** in his own signature, where the index says SERENA; the index gives him a father, 'Spouses Carlos', where *** THE CARD'S FATHER FIELD IS STRUCK THROUGH WITH A PEN *** and the indexer took CARLOS from the son's own forename; and the index puts his birth at *** Mendoza *** where the card says *** CAP. FEDERAL ***. *** AND IT BEARS ON THE CENTRAL QUESTION: *** these clerks CANCELLED a parent they did not know. source: Flores (Uruguay), Civil Registration - Death Records 1888-1917, acta No. 9 of 28 July 1911, Sexta seccion, before Esteban Indarte, Juez de Paz; image 271, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-Q7WL; plate read at full resolution

A priest drew that parentage in 1858; a Juez de Paz wrote it in 1911. *** IT ALSO NAMES HER FOUR SURVIVING CHILDREN - CASIMIRA JOSEFA, MALBINO HIPOLITO, MARIA INOCENCIA, JUAN FABIAN *** - three of whom this archive held as separate people from separate acts, and *** IT CORRECTS HER BIRTH YEAR BY ELEVEN YEARS *** and her birthplace. *** HER HUSBAND IS JUAN PEDRO PELAEZ ***, not simply Juan, and the declarant is her grandson.

source: Flores (Uruguay), Civil Registration - Death Records March 1918-January 1919 (the volume runs past its title), acta of 28 January 1926 at Estacion Juan Jose Castro; image 85, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-QNVC; plate read at full resolution

Abuelos paternos: ALEJANDRO LERENA y MARGARITA FERNANDEZ ***'. *** SO ALEJANDRO LERENA THE YOUNGER'S OWN PARENTAGE IS CONFIRMED BY A SECOND ACT SEVENTY-TWO YEARS AFTER THE EXPEDIENTE THAT FIRST GAVE IT. *** *** A THIRD SPELLING OF ISIDORA'S SURNAME *** - CHONZENO, CHOURINO, CHOUSINA - and none is preferred here. *** NOTE THE VOLUME'S TITLE IS WRONG FOR ITS CONTENTS ***, which is worth knowing before trusting a date range on this series.

used_for: *** WHERE FIDEL LERENA'S BURIAL WOULD BE, 9 November 2026: A MAP, NOT A SEARCH. *** The catalogue's film note for the cathedral's parish registers (koha 961086) lists 'Matrimonios, 1902-1934 -- Defunciones, 1729-1833 (incluye lista de difuntos de las invasiones inglesas)' on film 007713384. Five sample images, looked at in the plate reader, give the order of the book: image 1500 and 1700 are of the 1700s, image 2600 is of March 1807, image 2800 of 31 August 1815 and image 2950 of 25 June 1819, about forty images a year, so 1820-1823 should lie at about images 2990-3120 (an estimate, to be checked on the plates). The book has no machine transcript (the full-text view does not carry it), and the record index holds no cathedral burial of the 1820s, so a burial of Fidel Lerena can only be found by walking those pages; none has been read for the name. The cathedral's index of deaths 1800-1948 is on film 007713387 and is another way in (not opened). *** READ AT THE PLATE, 9 November 2026 (after the map above): NO FIDEL LERENA OR LLERENA IN THE ENTRIES AND MARGIN NAMES OF IMAGES 3019-3098 (16 December 1820 to 6 January 1824). *** Layout learned on the way: the volume of 1821-22 (film label 'Volumen 11', the last entry 15 May 1822) ends at image 3063; 3064 is blank and 3065 is the end-of-item card; image 3066 is the label of Volumen 12 and 3067 a filming note ('Libro grande'); images 3068-3069 are the cover and the title page, 'Libro 8o de Finados, empieza en 16 de Mayo de 1822', and the first entries are on image 3070. So every burial from 16 December 1820 to 6 January 1824 has been looked at (the left page of image 3031, early April 1821, is smudged and only partly legible; a few other pages of 1821 are faint) (image 3092 is a second exposure of 3091), two openings to an image, margin name and entry, at about the size of the plate reader (three images to a plate from 3019 on, and again from 3072: the margin names and the dates were read, a stray surname in the body of an entry may not have been). Not read: everything before image 3019 and after 3110 (from about 31 May 1824; images 3099-3110, 7 January to 30 May 1824, pp. 29-38, were read on 10 November 2026 with no Lerena or Llerena, a duplicate exposure and a pasted slip of May 1829 at p. 34 included; the book runs about four images to six weeks) (and, perhaps, a few days of January 1822 between the end of image 3053 at about 10 January and the start of 3054 at about 17 January, which I did not check against the page numbers); so this is a partial walk of one book, not a nil for Fidel. Terms looked for: Lerena, Llerena, Lerena misspelt as Larena/Lorena/Serena in a margin name; the Atlas cover check was not run. The book is the cathedral's only; a burial in Canelones, Las Piedras or Pando would not be here. *** READ TO THE END OF THE BOOK, 11 November 2026: NO FIDEL LERENA OR LLERENA, AND NO OTHER LERENA-TYPE SURNAME, IN THE ENTRIES, MARGIN NAMES, PARENTS OR WITNESSES OF IMAGES 3111-3310 (about 31 May 1824 to the last burial entry of January 1833). *** Layout of this stretch: two openings to an image, margin names surname-first or forename-first, entries 'se enterro en el Cementerio de esta Iglesia Matriz', signed by the cura (Gabriel Ibarguet in 1831, Francisco de Lazo from May 1831); 'Hospital de Caridad' deaths are entered in monthly blocks among the burials; images 3233 = 3232, 3244 = 3245 and 3307 = 3308 are second exposures of the same opening (counted once); the last burial page is p. 231 (image 3309, January 1833); image 3310 is a heading leaf, 'Siguen las partidas de los finados en el Hospital en el Libro 9o hacia el fin dando principio al mes de Febrero', with the right-hand page blank; image 3311 is the 'Fin del item' card (Montevideo, Archivos Parroquiales, P. Inm. Concep. (Catedral), Libros de Defunciones, Volumen 12, project URUG 1000A, roll 95), 3312 a Genealogical Society resolution chart, 3313-3314 'Fin del rollo' and 'End of roll'. So the burials of the cathedral on this film end in January 1833 and the hospital continuation the heading announces is not on the film. Terms looked for in every margin name and entry: Lerena, Llerena, Gerena, Lereña, Leresa, Lerina, Levena, Lorena, Serena, Sereña, Loreña, Larena, Perena, Lerama (the Atlas cover check for these exited 0 on 11 November 2026), and Fidel as a forename. Near-names seen and not counted: Lima Cordoso (Jose Antonio, p. 219, 4 December 1831, zoomed at image 3296), Guenechea, Larranaga, Fidel Vinals, Leyra, another Fidel (a Protestant native of North America, image 3178, surname unsettled), an infant Fidel Julian (image 3178), and an Arena who owned an enslaved woman (image 3168, not zoomed). THIS IS A READING NULL, NOT A WALKED BOOK AND NOT A NIL FOR FIDEL: the book was read two openings to a plate, margin names and dates, not transcribed; images before 3019 (the burials before 16 December 1820) are unread; a burial elsewhere (Canelones, Las Piedras, Pando, the country, a hospital or military record, or in a parish other than the cathedral) would not be here; and the cathedral's index of deaths (film 007713387) is still unopened. source: Archivo Diocesano de Getafe, inventory sheet for Valdemoro (Ntra. Sra. de la Asuncion), sacramental books; read as a published PDF, 13 November 2026 (not a register)
used_for: *** LOCATED, NOT SEARCHED: THE PARISH BOOKS OF VALDEMORO THAT COULD HOLD RAMON SERENA'S BAPTISM (ABOUT 1775-85) AND THE MARRIAGE OF SALVADOR SERENA AND ANA DE CUBAS ARE IN THE DIOCESAN ARCHIVE OF GETAFE, NOT ON FAMILYSEARCH. *** The archive's published inventory for Valdemoro lists: baptism books no. 16 (1752-1771, 378 folios), no. 17 (1772-1787, 262 folios), no. 18 (1787-1804, 408 folios) and no. 19 (1804-1816), none with an index; marriage books no. 8 (1724-1752), no. 9 (1752-1787, 290 folios), no. 10 (1787-1817, 269 folios), none indexed, and a separate marriage-index book for 1564-1822 (no folio count given); burial (difuntos) books no. 17 (1737-1745), 18 (1745-1763), 19 (1765-1797), 20 (1797-1818) and a children's burial book (parvulos) 1753-1788 and 1788-1812. It adds that marriage files (expedientes) and burial licences also exist. What this settles: the books exist and are kept at Getafe (the diocese since 1991; the archive holds the parish records of forty-eight towns); the 1812 Montevideo baptism act gives Ramon as natural de Valdemoro, his parents Salvador Serena and Ana de Cubas, so baptism book 17 (1772-1787) and marriage books 8-9 are the first to ask for, and the marriage-index book is the cheapest first look. What it does not settle: whether the archive allows a personal visit, a copy, or a search by letter, its fees, or whether the books are digitised; the inventory does not say, and no name was searched in any book. Spelling to ask for: Serena (as the act writes it) and Lerena, Gerena (as the Uruguayan indexes write it). This inventory is not a nil about any person. FamilySearch's own catalogue holds no Valdemoro parish registers (checked earlier, see data/1812-union-act.tsv).

source: Open-web search (two queries) for Comandante Pedro Antonio Llerena of the Spanish guerrillas, Canelones, 1820; and the full text of Julio Lerena Juanico, Cronica de un hogar montevideano (archive.org)
used_for: *** NOTHING FOUND ON THE OPEN WEB: NO PAGE NAMES A COMANDANTE PEDRO ANTONIO LLERENA OF 1820 IN CANELONES OR THE BANDA ORIENTAL. *** A narrow nil: two general web searches (the name with comandante, 1820, Canelones, Banda Oriental, guerrillas, Artigas, Lecor) returned only histories of the Portuguese conquest and the Canelones militias (Manuel Francisco Artigas, Felipe Duarte) and none named Llerena; the full text of Cronica de un hogar montevideano names Lerena only in its author credit (Julio Lerena Juanico). The sources that could still decide it were NOT searched: the Archivo General de la Nacion (Uruguay), the Archivo Historico Departamental de Canelones, the Archivo General Militar of Segovia and the Servicio Historico Militar, the Brazilian and Portuguese military records of the Cisplatine army, and PARES; none is searchable by name from here. The burial of 2 April 1820 (Canelones cathedral, image 192) remains the only record of him; whether he is the Pedro Antonio Lerena (son of Sancho, b. about 1793) of the Matriz marriage of 1861 is not established and not claimed. Terms: Llerena, Lerena, Pedro Antonio, comandante. Method: no control available.

The family of the name (written Ysauzzalde, Ysauzzaldi, Ysauzzal, Zauzzal, Yzauzal): (1) Francisco Ysauzzal and Magdalena Baez (Baes, Bais), at the Arroyo de la Cruz and 'otro lado del Lyji': Maria Josefa (29 January 1791), Maria Antonia (28 November 1792, godfather Lorenzo Villarreal) and Ysidora Josefa (24 January 1798, the same godfather); the 1805 act names them as the maternal grandparents of Paula, daughter of Fermin Medina and Dionisia (Dionicia) Ysauzzal, baptised 23 June 1805 (frame 212, zoomed), and acts of 11 October 1806 (frame 221) and 24 January 1807 (frame 225) name them as the maternal grandparents of the children of Maria Ysauzzal (wife of Salvador Soria) and of Polinaria Antonia Ysauzzal (wife of Leandro Aliendro, 'natural del Paraguay'), so Dionisia, Maria and Polinaria are their daughters, as Ysidora Josefa's parents have the same names; (2) Juan (Pascual) Ysauzzaldi and Juliana (written Hermosa, Hermosi, Verboi and Mocillo), at the Arroyo de la Virgen and the Arroyo de la Cruz: Wenceslao Miguel (1791), Felipa (buried 17 September 1796, aged 4 months, burial book frame 20, zoomed), Pedro Juan (1798) and Dominga (1799); (3) Fermin Medina and Dionisia: Calixto (buried 16 October 1796, burial book frame 21, zoomed), Hipolita (1798), Petrona Albina (1799), Paula (1805); (4) Salvador Soria and Maria Ysauzzaldi: Juan Pascual (1791), Maria Narcisa (1793), Petrona Josefa (1795), Maria Josefa (5 January 1798, frame 166, zoomed), Ignacia (1799), Petrona (1801), Domicilia (1803), Angela (1806); (5) Leandro Aliendro and Polinaria Antonia Ysauzzaldi: Feliciana Antonia (1797), Vicenta (1798), Felipe Andres (1800), Jacinta Michaela (1802), Tereza (1803), Pedro (1805), Ynocencia Josefa (1806); and Ines Ysauzzal (wife of Rosendo Guerreros), Josefa Ysauzzal, Josef, Claudio, Wenceslao, Miguel, Cornelio Cipriano and Maria Josefa Columba Ysauzzal, named as godparents or parents without a stated link. Not read: frames 1-119 and 226 onwards of this film (the book runs on far past 1807).
